body.en:
jQuery is a fast, small and feature-rich JavaScript library. Its motto is "Write less, do more". It makes common JavaScript tasks such as selecting HTML elements, handling events, creating animations and making AJAX calls much easier, with short code that works the same in all browsers.

  • Created by John Resig and released in January 2006.
  • Free and open source (MIT licence), maintained by the OpenJS Foundation.
  • A library is a collection of ready-made functions. jQuery is a single JavaScript file (about 30 KB minified and compressed).
  • Current version used in these notes: jQuery 3.7.1.

What jQuery can do

  • HTML/DOM manipulation: read and change content, attributes and elements.
  • CSS manipulation: change styles and classes.
  • Event handling: click, keyup, submit, resize and more.
  • Effects and animations: hide, show, fade, slide, animate.
  • AJAX: load data from the server without reloading the page.
  • Utilities and a large number of plug-ins (sliders, date pickers, validation).

Including jQuery in a page

jQuery must be added with a <script> tag before any script that uses it. It can be loaded from a CDN (Content Delivery Network) or from a downloaded local file (jquery-3.7.1.min.js from jquery.com).

<!-- 1. from a CDN -->
<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.7.1.min.js">
</script>

<!-- 2. from a local file -->
<script src="js/jquery-3.7.1.min.js"></script>

<!-- your own code AFTER jQuery -->
<script src="js/script.js"></script>

The .min.js (minified) version has spaces and comments removed, so it downloads faster; the uncompressed version is used for reading and debugging.

Why jQuery became important

  • Write less, do more: one line of jQuery often replaces many lines of JavaScript.
  • Cross-browser compatibility: jQuery hides the differences between browsers, so the same code works everywhere.
  • Easy DOM selection: uses CSS selectors that web designers already know.
  • Simple event handling and built-in animations without writing timers.
  • Easy AJAX with $.ajax(), $.get(), load().
  • Method chaining: many actions on the same element in one statement.
  • Huge plug-in ecosystem, good documentation and a large community.
  • Used by many websites and older frameworks: Bootstrap 3 and 4 needed jQuery for their JavaScript components; WordPress still includes it.

jQuery vs plain JavaScript

// Plain JavaScript
document.getElementById("msg")
        .style.display = "none";

// jQuery
$("#msg").hide();
JavaScriptjQuery
A programming languageA library written in JavaScript
Longer code for DOM tasksShort, readable code
Browser differences must be handledCross-browser handled by jQuery
No extra file; fastestNeeds the jQuery file; slightly slower

Limitations

  • An extra file must be downloaded.
  • Modern JavaScript (querySelector, fetch, classList) now does many jQuery tasks, so new frameworks (and Bootstrap 5) do not depend on it.

The basic jQuery syntax selects HTML elements and performs an action on them:

$(selector).action()

  • $ is a short name for the jQuery function (jQuery("p") = $("p")).
  • (selector) finds HTML elements, using CSS selector syntax.
  • action() is a jQuery method performed on the selected elements.
$(selector).action();

$(this).hide();      // current element
$("p").hide();       // all <p> elements
$(".test").hide();   // all with class="test"
$("#test").hide();   // element with id="test"

The document ready event

jQuery code is normally written inside the document ready function. It runs only after the whole HTML document (the DOM) has been loaded, so that all elements exist before we try to use them. Without it, code in the <head> would try to select elements that are not created yet.

$(document).ready(function () {
  // jQuery code here
});

// short form
$(function () {
  // jQuery code here
});
  • $(document).ready() runs when the DOM is ready (before images finish loading).
  • $(window).on("load", fn) waits until images and all other files are loaded too.

Method chaining

Most jQuery methods return the same jQuery object, so several methods can be joined: $("#p1").css("color", "red").slideUp(500).slideDown(500);

Getters and setters

The same method reads or writes depending on the arguments: $("#a").val() gets the value, $("#a").val("5") sets it. The same is true for text(), html(), attr() and css().

Selectors are used to find (select) HTML elements by their name, id, class, attributes, type, position and more. jQuery selectors are based on CSS selectors, plus some extra filters of its own. All selectors start with the dollar sign and parentheses: $().

1. Element selector

Selects elements by tag name: $("p") selects all paragraphs.

2. #id selector

Selects the single element with a given id: $("#roll"). An id must be unique in a page, so this is the fastest selector.

3. .class selector

Selects all elements with a given class: $(".note").

4. Other selectors

$("*")                 // all elements
$("p")                 // element
$("#roll")             // id
$(".note")             // class
$("h1, h2, p")         // group
$("ul li")             // descendant
$("ul > li")           // direct child
$("[href]")            // has attribute
$("[type='text']")     // attribute value
$("a[href^='https']")  // value starts with
$("li:first")          // first match
$("tr:even")           // index 0, 2, 4 ...
$("li:eq(2)")          // index 2
$(":button")           // all buttons
TypeMeaning
Universal *Every element
Group (comma)Elements matching any of the selectors
Descendant (space) / child (>)Elements inside another element
Attribute [ ]Elements with an attribute or attribute value (=, ^= starts with, $= ends with, *= contains)
Filters :first, :last, :even, :odd, :eq(n)Select by position (index starts at 0)
Form filters :button, :input, :checkedSelect form elements by type or state
$(this)The element that fired the current event

Note: :first, :even and :eq() are deprecated from jQuery 3.4 but still work; the recommended methods are .first(), .even() and .eq(n).

An event is an action the page can respond to, such as clicking a button, moving the mouse over an element, pressing a key, submitting a form or resizing the window. The moment an event happens is called firing; the function that responds is the event handler.

$(selector).event(function (e) {
  // code runs when the event occurs
});

$("#btn").click(function () {
  $("p").hide();
});

Common DOM events

MouseKeyboardFormDocument / window
clickkeydownsubmitready
dblclickkeyupchangeload
mouseenterkeypressfocusresize
mouseleaveblurscroll

Important event methods

  • click() / dblclick(): single or double click.
  • mouseenter() / mouseleave(): pointer enters / leaves the element. hover(in, out) combines both.
  • keydown() / keyup(): key pressed / released.
  • focus() / blur(): a field gets / loses the cursor.
  • change(): the value of a select, checkbox or input changes.
  • submit(): a form is submitted.
  • on(): attaches one or more events; off() removes them.
$("#box").hover(
  function () { $(this).css("color", "red"); },
  function () { $(this).css("color", "black"); }
);
// one event
$("#btn").on("click", function () { ... });

// several events, one handler
$("#box").on("mouseenter mouseleave",
  function () { $(this).toggleClass("hi"); });

// delegation (works for new elements)
$("#list").on("click", "li", function () {
  $(this).remove();
});

$("#btn").off("click");  // remove handler

The event object

jQuery passes an event object to the handler. Useful members: e.type (event name), e.target (element), e.pageX / e.pageY (mouse position), e.which or e.key (key pressed), e.preventDefault() (stop default action, e.g. form submit or link) and e.stopPropagation() (stop the event from reaching parent elements).

$("#form1").submit(function (e) {
  e.preventDefault();   // do not reload
  var n = $("#name").val();
  if (n === "") alert("Enter name");
});

Effects

MethodEffect
hide(), show(), toggle()Hide / show elements
fadeIn(), fadeOut(), fadeToggle(), fadeTo()Change opacity gradually
slideDown(), slideUp(), slideToggle()Change height gradually
animate({css}, speed)Custom animation of numeric CSS properties
stop()Stop a running animation

The speed can be "slow", "fast" or milliseconds. A callback function runs after the effect is complete.

$("#p1").hide(400);
$("#p1").show("slow");
$("#p1").toggle();
$("#p1").fadeIn(); $("#p1").fadeOut();
$("#p1").fadeToggle(); $("#p1").fadeTo(500, 0.4);
$("#p1").slideDown(); $("#p1").slideUp();
$("#p1").slideToggle(300, function () {
  alert("done");   // callback
});
$("#b").animate({ left: "200px",
                  opacity: 0.5 }, 1000);

DOM manipulation

  • Get/set content: text(), html(), val().
  • Attributes: attr(), removeAttr(), data().
  • Add elements: append() (end, inside), prepend() (start, inside), after(), before() (outside).
  • Remove elements: remove() (the element itself), empty() (only its children).
  • CSS classes: addClass(), removeClass(), toggleClass(), hasClass(); css() for inline style.
  • Traversing: parent(), children(), find(), next(), prev(), siblings().
$("#p1").text();              // get text
$("#p1").text("Hello");       // set text
$("#p1").html("<b>Hi</b>");   // set HTML
$("#name").val();             // get input value
$("a").attr("href", "#top");  // set attribute
$("ul").append("<li>end</li>");
$("ul").prepend("<li>start</li>");
$("#p1").after("<hr>");
$("#p1").remove();   $("ul").empty();
$("p").addClass("big");
$("p").removeClass("big");
$("p").toggleClass("big");
$("p").css("color", "blue");

h.en: What is Bootstrap and Why Use It?

body.en:
Bootstrap is a free and open-source front-end framework for designing responsive, mobile-first websites and web applications. It contains ready-made HTML and CSS design templates for typography, forms, buttons, tables, navigation, cards, modals, image carousels and more, plus optional JavaScript plug-ins.

  • A framework gives a ready structure and rules; we build our page by adding Bootstrap classes to normal HTML elements, e.g. class="btn btn-primary".
  • Website: getbootstrap.com. Latest major version: Bootstrap 5 (5.3.3 used here).

Why use Bootstrap?

  • Saves time: no need to write CSS for common components; they are ready.
  • Responsive by default: the same page fits mobiles, tablets and desktops.
  • Mobile first: styles are designed for small screens first.
  • Consistent design across all pages and team members.
  • Browser compatibility: works in all modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera).
  • Easy to learn: only basic HTML and CSS knowledge is needed.

Example: centring text with and without Bootstrap

Without Bootstrap we write our own flexbox CSS and media queries (Practical 2a). With Bootstrap the same result needs only classes (Practical 2b):

<div class="d-flex min-vh-100
  justify-content-center align-items-center
  text-center">
  <h1>Government Polytechnic</h1>
</div>

• 2010: developed at Twitter by Mark Otto and Jacob Thornton as an internal tool called Twitter Blueprint, to keep the design of Twitter's internal tools consistent.
  • 19 August 2011: released as an open-source project on GitHub with the name Bootstrap (originally "Twitter Bootstrap").
  • Bootstrap 2 (January 2012): added responsive design with a 12-column fluid grid and Glyphicons.
  • Bootstrap 3 (August 2013): rewritten to be mobile first, flat design, grid classes xs/sm/md/lg; panels, thumbnails, wells and jumbotron. It needed jQuery.
  • Bootstrap 4 (January 2018): moved from Less to Sass, Flexbox grid, rem units, new xl breakpoint; cards replaced panels, wells and thumbnails; Glyphicons dropped.
  • Bootstrap 5 (May 2021): jQuery removed (pure JavaScript), Internet Explorer support dropped, new xxl breakpoint, RTL support, Utility API, improved forms, Bootstrap Icons library, data-bs-* attributes.
  • Bootstrap 5.3 (2023): colour modes (dark mode) with the data-bs-theme attribute.

Bootstrap is one of the most popular projects on GitHub and is used by millions of websites.

The GTU syllabus mentions some Bootstrap 3 components (panel, jumbotron, thumbnail, affix, glyphicons). These notes use Bootstrap 5 and show the modern replacement for each old item.

FeatureBootstrap 3Bootstrap 4Bootstrap 5
CSS sourceLessSassSass
Gridfloatflexboxflexbox (+ CSS grid option)
Breakpointsxs, sm, md, lg+ xl+ xxl
jQueryrequiredrequirednot needed
IconsGlyphiconsnone built-inBootstrap Icons (separate)
Panels, wells, thumbnailsyesreplaced by cardcard
Jumbotronyesyesremoved (use utilities)
Affix plug-inyesremoved (use sticky-top)sticky-top
Data attributesdata-toggledata-toggledata-bs-toggle
Internet ExplorerIE 8+IE 10+not supported

Using jQuery with Bootstrap 5

Bootstrap 5 does not need jQuery, but jQuery can still be added for our own scripts. jQuery handles events and creates elements, Bootstrap gives the styling. Bootstrap 5.3 also supports dark mode:

<html lang="en" data-bs-theme="dark">

1. Responsive grid system: a 12-column flexbox grid with six breakpoints makes layouts adapt automatically.
  2. Mobile-first approach: pages are designed for phones first and enhanced for larger screens.
  3. Pre-styled components: buttons, navbars, cards, forms, alerts, badges, modals, carousels and many more.
  4. Fast development: classes are added instead of writing CSS, saving time.
  5. Consistency: the same look on every page, by every developer.
  6. Cross-browser compatibility: tested on all modern browsers.
  7. JavaScript plug-ins ready to use with data attributes, no coding needed.
  8. Customisable: Sass variables, maps and the Utility API allow own colours, fonts and themes; unused parts can be removed.
  9. Utility classes for spacing, colours, display, flex, borders, shadows.
  10. Free and open source, excellent documentation, huge community, many free themes and templates.

Disadvantages

  • Many websites look similar if the default style is not customised.
  • The CSS file is large if the whole library is used.
  • HTML can contain many classes (class-heavy markup).
  • Learning the class names takes some time, and overriding default styles can be difficult.

Bootstrap can be added to a web page in two common ways (a third way is installing it with a package manager such as npm install bootstrap).

Method 1: Using a CDN

A CDN (Content Delivery Network) is a network of servers that delivers files from the server nearest to the user. Bootstrap's official CDN is jsDelivr. No download is required, and the file may already be cached in the browser, but an internet connection is needed.

<link rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css">

<script
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js">
</script>

Method 2: Downloading Bootstrap (local files)

  1. Go to getbootstrap.com and click Download (compiled CSS and JS).
  2. Extract the zip file. It contains the css and js folders.
  3. Copy bootstrap.min.css and bootstrap.bundle.min.js into the project folders.
  4. Link them from the HTML page with relative paths.
my_site/
  index.html
  css/
    bootstrap.min.css
  js/
    bootstrap.bundle.min.js
  images/

Basic Bootstrap template (Practical 1)

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport"
    content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My first Bootstrap page</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/bootstrap.min.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container">
    <h1>Hello, world!</h1>
  </div>
  <script src="js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
  • <!DOCTYPE html>: Bootstrap requires the HTML5 doctype.
  • Viewport meta tag: needed for responsive behaviour on mobiles.
  • CSS is linked in <head>; the JavaScript bundle is placed just before </body> so the page appears first.
  • bootstrap.bundle.min.js includes Popper (used to position dropdowns, tooltips and popovers). If bootstrap.min.js is used instead, Popper must be added separately.
  • Content is placed inside a .container (fixed width per breakpoint) or .container-fluid (full width).
  • To install Bootstrap Icons, link bootstrap-icons.min.css the same way.

Responsive web design (RWD) is an approach in which a web page automatically adjusts its layout, images and text to the size of the screen (mobile, tablet, laptop, desktop), so it is easy to read and use without zooming or horizontal scrolling. The term was introduced by Ethan Marcotte in 2010.

Main ingredients

  1. Viewport meta tag, so the browser uses the device width.
  2. Fluid grid: widths in percentages instead of fixed pixels.
  3. Flexible images: max-width: 100% (Bootstrap class img-fluid).
  4. Media queries: different CSS rules for different screen widths.
/* plain CSS media query */
.box { width: 100%; }
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .box { width: 50%; }
}

Responsive page with Bootstrap

Bootstrap gives all four ingredients. Its grid has 12 columns in each row; a column class tells how many of the 12 columns an element uses at each breakpoint:

<div class="container">
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-12 col-sm-6 col-lg-3">A</div>
    <div class="col-12 col-sm-6 col-lg-3">B</div>
    <div class="col-12 col-sm-6 col-lg-3">C</div>
    <div class="col-12 col-sm-6 col-lg-3">D</div>
  </div>
</div>
  • col-12: full width (1 per row) on extra-small screens.
  • col-sm-6: half width (2 per row) from 576 px.
  • col-lg-3: one quarter (4 per row) from 992 px.

Steps to create a responsive page

  1. Start from the basic template with the viewport tag and Bootstrap linked.
  2. Wrap content in .container, then .row, then .col-*.
  3. Choose column classes for each breakpoint (mobile first).
  4. Use img-fluid for images and responsive utilities (d-none, d-md-block) to hide or show parts.
  5. Test by resizing the browser or with the browser's device toolbar (F12).

The viewport meta tag

The viewport is the visible area of a web page on the screen. Mobile browsers, by default, render a page at a virtual width of about 980 px and then shrink it to fit the phone, so text becomes tiny. The viewport meta tag tells the browser to use the actual width of the device.

<meta name="viewport"
  content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  • width=device-width: set the page width equal to the screen width of the device.
  • initial-scale=1: set the zoom level to 100% when the page is first loaded.
  • Other options: maximum-scale, minimum-scale, user-scalable=no (not recommended, it stops users from zooming).

Bootstrap 5 breakpoints

Breakpoints are the screen widths at which the layout changes. They are used in class names as infixes, e.g. col-md-6, d-lg-none.

BreakpointClass infixWidth
Extra small(none)< 576 px
Smallsm>= 576 px
Mediummd>= 768 px
Largelg>= 992 px
Extra largexl>= 1200 px
Extra extra largexxl>= 1400 px

Bootstrap uses min-width media queries, so a class applies at its breakpoint and above. This is why Bootstrap is called mobile first.

Every Bootstrap layout starts with a container. The container width changes at each breakpoint:

Classxssmmdlgxlxxl
.container100%540px720px960px1140px1320px
.container-sm100%540px720px960px1140px1320px
.container-md100%100%720px960px1140px1320px
.container-lg100%100%100%960px1140px1320px
.container-fluid100%100%100%100%100%100%
  • .container: responsive fixed-width box, centred on the page.
  • .container-fluid: always 100% wide.
  • .container-{breakpoint}: 100% wide until the breakpoint, then fixed width.

Grid and container details are studied in Unit 2.

Sometimes a page must keep a fixed desktop layout on all devices, for example an internal admin page or a report. Bootstrap is responsive by default, so the following steps are used to disable responsiveness:

  1. Remove the viewport meta tag. Mobile browsers then show the page at desktop width and zoom it out.
  2. Override the container width with a fixed value and set max-width: none !important, so it does not shrink at breakpoints.
  3. Use grid classes without breakpoints (.col-4 instead of .col-md-4), so columns never stack.
  4. For a navbar, remove the collapse and toggler (or use navbar-expand, which never collapses).
  5. Avoid responsive utility classes such as d-md-none.
<!-- 1. no viewport meta tag -->
<style>
  /* 2. fixed width container */
  .container {
    width: 970px !important;
    max-width: none !important;
  }
</style>
<!-- 3. grid classes without breakpoints -->
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-4">...</div>
  <div class="col-4">...</div>
  <div class="col-4">...</div>
</div>

Result: on a phone the user sees a small, zoomed-out page and must zoom or scroll sideways. This is why responsiveness should be removed only when it is really needed.

1. Responsive grid system: 12 columns, 6 breakpoints, flexbox based; offsets, ordering and nesting.
  2. Mobile-first styles throughout the framework.
  3. Reboot and typography: consistent default styles for headings, lists, tables, display headings, lead text.
  4. Components: buttons, button groups, navs, navbar, breadcrumb, pagination, badges, alerts, cards, list groups, progress bars, spinners, toasts, forms and input groups.
  5. JavaScript plug-ins: modal, dropdown, collapse, carousel, tooltip, popover, scrollspy, tab, offcanvas, toast; used with data-bs-* attributes or JavaScript.
  6. Utility classes: spacing (m-3, p-2), colours, display, flex, borders, shadows, sizing, position, text.
  7. Forms: styled controls, floating labels, validation styles.
  8. Icons: Bootstrap Icons, an open-source library of 2000+ SVG icons.
  9. Customisation: Sass variables, maps, mixins, CSS variables, the Utility API and colour modes (dark mode).
  10. Browser compatibility and accessibility (ARIA attributes, keyboard support).
  11. Documentation and community: clear official docs with examples; free and open source (MIT licence).

title.en: First jQuery program: document ready, hide and show

code.en:
Welcome to jQuery

This paragraph can be hidden and shown again using jQuery.

programs.out:
A heading, a lavender paragraph and three buttons. Below them the green text "jQuery is ready!" appears as soon as the page loads.
Hide makes the paragraph disappear, Show brings it back, and Toggle hides or shows it with a 0.4 second animation.

expl.en:
• The jQuery library is included with <script src="js/jquery-3.7.1.min.js"> before our own script. (From a CDN: https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.7.1.min.js.)
  • $(document).ready(function () { ... }); runs the code only after the whole HTML document (DOM) is loaded, so all elements exist. The short form is $(function () { ... });
  • Basic syntax: $(selector).action(). $("#msg") selects the element with id="msg", and .hide() is the action.
  • .click(function) attaches a click event handler. .text("...") sets the text of an element.
  • toggle(400) hides a visible element or shows a hidden one; 400 is the animation time in milliseconds.

title.en: jQuery selectors: element, id, class, attribute and filters

code.en:
jQuery Selectors

Paragraph 1 (element selector)

Paragraph 2 has class="note"

Paragraph 3 has id="special"

  • HTML
  • CSS
  • JavaScript
  • jQuery
  • Bootstrap

External | Internal

programs.out:
All paragraphs get a grey border, the one with class "note" gets an orange background and the one with id "special" turns red.
In the list, HTML is bold; HTML, JavaScript and Bootstrap (positions 0, 2, 4) get a light blue background, and "(last)" is added after Bootstrap.
The password box gets a green border and the external link turns orange. The heading and Paragraph 3 are italic.

expl.en:
• Element selector $("p") selects all <p> elements.
  • Class selector $(".note") selects elements with class="note". Id selector $("#special") selects the one element with id="special".
  • Filters: :first gives the first match; :even gives positions 0, 2, 4 ... (counting starts at 0). :last-child is a CSS selector that also works.
  • Attribute selector [type='password'] matches an attribute value; [href^='https'] matches values that start with https.
  • Group selector $("h2, #special") selects both. .css(property, value) changes a style, and .append() adds content at the end.

title.en: Mouse events: click, dblclick, mouseenter, mouseleave

code.en:
Mouse Events

Point at me, click me or double-click me

Event log (newest first):

programs.out:
A lavender box. When the mouse enters it, the box turns light orange; when the mouse leaves, it turns lavender again.
Every event is added at the top of the numbered "Event log", e.g. 1. dblclick - text size changed, 2. click, 3. click, 4. mouseenter.
A double-click makes the text bigger (and smaller again on the next double-click). On a phone a tap gives a click event.

expl.en:
• An event is an action of the user (or browser) that the page can respond to. In jQuery: $(selector).event(function () { ... });
  • mouseenter / mouseleave fire when the pointer moves into / out of the element. hover(fnIn, fnOut) is a shortcut for both.
  • click and dblclick fire on single and double clicks. A double-click also fires two click events first, as the log shows.
  • Inside a handler, this is the element that received the event; $(this) wraps it as a jQuery object.
  • prepend() inserts content at the beginning; toggleClass("big") adds the class if missing and removes it if present.

title.en: Keyboard and form events: focus, blur, keyup, change, submit

code.en:
Feedback Form

0 / 50

programs.out:
A feedback form with Name, Feedback, Branch and a Submit button.
The box you are typing in turns light yellow, and white again when you leave it. While you type feedback, the counter shows e.g. "12 / 50".
Choosing a branch shows "You selected: Computer". Submit with an empty name shows a red "Please enter your name"; with a name it shows a green "Thank you, Riya" and the page is not reloaded.

expl.en:
• focus fires when an input gets the cursor and blur when it loses it. jQuery methods can be chained: .focus(...).blur(...).
  • keyup fires when a key is released; .val() reads the current value, so the length is counted on every key press. (Other keyboard events: keydown, keypress.)
  • change fires when the selected option of a <select> (or a checkbox, radio or input value) changes.
  • submit fires when the form is submitted. e.preventDefault() stops the browser from sending the form and reloading the page, so we can validate it first.
  • .trim() removes spaces from both ends, so a name of only spaces is also treated as empty.

title.en: on() method, event object and window resize

code.en:
Screen width: px

Device type:

Resize the browser window (or switch to desktop view) to see the values change.

programs.out:
The heading shows the current width of the browser window, e.g. "Screen width: 390 px", and the device type "Mobile (xs)" (on a desktop browser of 1100 px: "Laptop (lg)").
The numbers update immediately when the window is resized. The Red, Green and Blue buttons change the colour of the heading and show "Event type: click, button: Green".

expl.en:
• .on(event, handler) is the general way to attach any event; .click(fn) is a shortcut for .on("click", fn). .off() removes handlers.
  • The resize event of $(window) fires whenever the browser size changes. $(window).width() gives the width in pixels.
  • The width limits 576, 768, 992 and 1200 px are the same breakpoints that Bootstrap uses for responsive layouts.
  • The handler receives an event object with details: event.type, event.target, event.pageX / pageY, event.which (key code).
  • .data("color") reads the custom attribute data-color; one handler serves all three buttons.

code.en:
Simple Calculator

Result:

programs.out:
Two number boxes and the buttons + - x / Clear.
Enter 25 and 4 and press x: the green line shows "Result: 100". Press / to get "Result: 6.25". With an empty box it shows "Result: Enter both numbers", and dividing by 0 shows "Result: Cannot divide by 0". Clear empties both boxes.

expl.en:
• .val() without an argument reads the value of an input; .val("") sets it. The same getter/setter rule applies to .text(), .html() and .css().
  • Input values are strings, so parseFloat() converts them to numbers; isNaN() checks for an empty or invalid entry.
  • $("button[data-op]") selects only buttons that have a data-op attribute, so the Clear button is handled separately.
  • One handler serves four buttons: $(this).data("op") tells which operator was pressed.

title.en: jQuery effects and DOM: slideToggle, append, fadeOut

code.en:
FAQ

What is jQuery?
A fast, small JavaScript library that makes DOM handling, events and animation easy.
Who created jQuery?
John Resig, in 2006.

expl.en:
• Effects: slideToggle(), slideUp(), slideDown(), fadeIn(), fadeOut(), fadeToggle(), animate(). The number is the speed in ms; a callback function runs after the effect ends.
  • $(this).next(".a") moves to the next sibling element with class "a" (DOM traversal).
  • append() creates new elements from an HTML string; remove() deletes elements.
  • Event delegation: $("#list").on("click", "li", fn) attaches one handler to the <ul> that also works for <li> items added later. A plain $("li").click() would not work for new items.

expl.en:
• <!DOCTYPE html> and lang are required for HTML5. <meta charset="UTF-8"> sets the character encoding.
  • The viewport meta tag width=device-width, initial-scale=1 makes the page use the real width of the device; without it a phone shows a zoomed-out desktop page.

title.en: Responsive web page: one layout for mobile, tablet and desktop

code.en:
Computer Engineering

Semester 1

C Programming

Semester 2

Semester 3

Web Page Design

Semester 4

Java Programming

Resize the window to see 1, 2 or 4 columns

programs.out:
A blue header "Computer Engineering", then four grey cards (Semester 1 to 4) and a footer.
On a phone (under 576 px) the cards are stacked one below the other; from 576 px they appear 2 per row; on a large screen (992 px and above, desktop view) all 4 cards sit in one row.

expl.en:
• A responsive web page adjusts its layout to the screen size, so it is easy to read on mobiles, tablets and desktops without zooming or horizontal scrolling.
  • Each card is in a column with three classes: col-12 (full width on extra-small screens), col-sm-6 (half width from 576 px) and col-lg-3 (quarter width from 992 px).
  • The grid has 12 columns per row: 12 = 1 card per row, 6 = 2 cards, 3 = 4 cards.
  • g-3 adds a gap (gutter) between columns; h-100 makes all cards in a row the same height.
  • Bootstrap is mobile first: the smallest-screen class is written first, and larger breakpoints override it.

code.en:
Non-responsive page

Column 1
Column 2
Column 3

The page is always 970 px wide. On a phone it is zoomed out or scrolls sideways.

programs.out:
The page is always 970 px wide with three coloured columns (yellow, light blue, green) side by side in one row.
On a phone the three columns do not stack: the whole page appears zoomed out (or must be scrolled sideways), like an old desktop-only website.

expl.en:
Sometimes a fixed desktop layout is required (e.g. an admin panel or a printed report). Steps to disable responsiveness in Bootstrap:

  1. Remove (or do not add) the <meta name="viewport"> tag. The phone browser then renders the page at about 980 px and zooms it out.
  2. Give .container a fixed width and override max-width with !important.
  3. Use grid classes without breakpoints (col-4, not col-md-4), so columns never stack.
  4. For a navbar, do not use the collapse/toggler; keep the menu always expanded.

Compare with the previous program, where the cards rearrange themselves on small screens.

title.en: jQuery with Bootstrap: dynamic alerts and dark mode

code.en: Notice Board

programs.out:
A "Notice Board" heading with a Dark mode switch, and an input box with a type list (Info / Success / Urgent) and a Post button.
Typing "Practical exam on Monday", choosing Urgent and pressing Post adds a red alert with a close (x) button at the top of the list; Info gives a light blue alert and Success a green one.
Turning on the switch changes the whole page to dark colours.

expl.en:
• jQuery and Bootstrap work well together: jQuery handles events and creates elements, Bootstrap provides the styling.
  • The new alert is built as an HTML string with the class alert-info, alert-success or alert-danger from the select box, and inserted with prepend().
  • The close button works even for alerts added later, because Bootstrap listens for data-bs-dismiss clicks on the whole document.
  • .attr("data-bs-theme", "dark") on the <html> element switches Bootstrap 5.3 to its dark colour mode.
  • Bootstrap 5 itself does not need jQuery (Bootstrap 3 and 4 did); jQuery is added here only for our own script.

a.en: A fast, small, cross-browser JavaScript library that simplifies DOM manipulation, event handling, animation and AJAX. Motto: write less, do more.
John Resig, released in January 2006.
No. It is a library written in JavaScript.
$ is a short name (alias) for the jQuery function. $("p") is the same as jQuery("p").

q.en: What is the basic syntax of jQuery?

a.en: $(selector).action(): select elements and perform an action on them.
To run jQuery code only after the DOM is fully loaded, so all elements exist.
ready fires when the DOM is ready; load waits until images and all other resources are loaded.

q.en: What are the two ways to include jQuery?

a.en: From a CDN (e.g. code.jquery.com) or from a downloaded local file.
A file with spaces, comments and long names removed to reduce its size, e.g. jquery-3.7.1.min.js.
Expressions used to find HTML elements by tag, id, class, attribute, position etc., based on CSS selectors.
The id selector ($("#id")), because an id is unique.
List items at index 0, 2, 4 ... (index counting starts at 0).
The jQuery object of the element on which the current event occurred.
An action such as a click, key press, mouse movement, form submit or window resize to which the page can respond.
click, dblclick, mouseenter, mouseleave, mousedown, mouseup, hover.
submit, change, focus, blur.

q.en: What is the difference between keydown and keyup?

a.en: keydown fires when a key is pressed down, keyup when it is released.

q.en: What is the use of the on() method?

a.en: To attach one or more event handlers to elements, including delegated events for elements added later.
Attaching a handler to a parent element that handles events of its (current and future) children.
Stops the browser's default action, e.g. a form reload or following a link.
Calling several jQuery methods one after another on the same selection in one statement.
text() gets/sets plain text; html() gets/sets content including HTML tags.
append() adds content at the end inside the element; prepend() at the beginning.
remove() deletes the element itself; empty() deletes only its child content.
hide, show, toggle, fadeIn, fadeOut, fadeToggle, slideUp, slideDown, slideToggle, animate.
A function that runs after another action (such as an effect) is complete.
A free, open-source front-end framework of HTML, CSS and JavaScript for building responsive, mobile-first websites.
Mark Otto and Jacob Thornton at Twitter; released as open source on 19 August 2011.
Twitter Blueprint (later Twitter Bootstrap).

q.en: What is the latest major version of Bootstrap?

a.en: Bootstrap 5 (released 2021); version 5.3 added dark mode.
No. Bootstrap 5 uses plain JavaScript. Bootstrap 3 and 4 needed jQuery.
Styles are designed for small screens first, then larger screens are enhanced using min-width media queries.
Designing pages whose layout adjusts automatically to different screen sizes and devices.
Content Delivery Network: a group of servers that deliver files (like Bootstrap) from the server nearest to the user.

q.en: Which files are needed to use Bootstrap?

a.en: bootstrap.min.css and, for interactive components, bootstrap.bundle.min.js.
Bootstrap's JavaScript plug-ins plus Popper, used to position dropdowns, tooltips and popovers.

q.en: Where are the CSS and JS files linked?

a.en: CSS in the head; JavaScript just before the closing body tag.

q.en: Why is the viewport meta tag used?

a.en: So that mobile browsers use the device width and initial zoom 1, which makes the page responsive.
The page width is set equal to the screen width of the device.

q.en: How many columns are in the Bootstrap grid?

a.en: 12 columns per row.
xs (below 576), sm 576, md 768, lg 992, xl 1200 and xxl 1400 pixels.
.container has a fixed maximum width at each breakpoint; .container-fluid is always 100% wide.
Remove the viewport meta tag, give the container a fixed width and use col-* classes without breakpoints.

q.en: Name some major features of Bootstrap.

a.en: Responsive grid, mobile first, ready components, JavaScript plug-ins, utility classes, icons, Sass customisation, browser compatibility.
Bootstrap Icons, a separate open-source SVG icon library.

q.en: What replaced panels, wells and thumbnails?

a.en: The card component (from Bootstrap 4).

q.en: What is a disadvantage of Bootstrap?

a.en: Websites can look similar, the file is large if everything is used, and HTML gets many classes.

q.en: How do you enable dark mode in Bootstrap 5.3?

a.en: Add data-bs-theme="dark" to the html element (or any element).
